cohort: The study included 90 children and adolescents aged 3 to 18 years with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) of at least 6 months duration.
finding: Conventional insulins and vial-syringes were the most commonly used insulin delivery systems, and better glycemic control (HbA1c <8%) was observed in younger age groups, those with shorter T1D duration, users of basal-bolus regimens, analog insulins, and pen devices.
